I farm sorghum here in the North East like my father did, and last season the rains came late so I am careful with my cash this year. I will buy one bag of NPK and maybe one bag of urea if the money comes through after I sell some of last year's groundnut — that is enough to spread thin across this plot since sorghum is not so hungry as maize. I keep my local sorghum seed from last harvest because it stands the dry spells better than the new ones the agro-dealer tries to sell me, and I put my goat manure on the plot before the first rains. My two sons help me weed and I will call two or three young men from the village for the first weeding when the grass comes fast.
